newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pressure mounting on landmine producers - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Pressure mounting on landmine producers - Red Cross.

text.p: An International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) representative on Friday said that nations that produce anti-personnel mines would not be able to hold out against a global ban on mines.

The weight of international opinion was gathering against nations such as China and Russia, which have refused to join international efforts towards a global ban on mines, ICRC spokesman Urs Boegli told reporters at the end of a two-day Tokyo Conference on Anti-Personnel Landmines.
"A weapon that a hundred countries use is easy to use. A weapon that fifteen countries use is delicate to use. A weapon that three or four countries use will be very difficult to use," he said.

China and Russia have not taken part in the "Ottawa talks" begun last October and aimed at a legally binding international ban on the production, stockpiling, export and use of land mines by this December. Major mine manufacturers the United States, Britain and France did attend.

U.N. Mine Clearance Unit chief John MacInnis said the Ottawa talks and a parallel U.S.-led initiative at the U.N. Conference on Disarmament would be ineffective without the eventual cooperation of China and Russia.

"Our object is to get (Russia and China) on board. The Ottawa process will help get these two on board by showing that there is a significant will that is being generated in support of the ban," he said.

MacInnis added that the Canadian representative to the conference had indicated there was significant support for the Ottawa process, and that it might serve as the focus for gathering international momentum towards a global ban if the U.N. talks became bogged down.

"The countries which are pushing for the Ottawa process are watching this very carefully to see how fast it is going to move, and some are ready to change direction if the Conference on Disarmament does not make significant progress," he said.

"But clearly, the Ottawa process will be an incentive for that one to continue if a significant number of countries sign up to the treaty that Ottawa is proposing to be signed in December 1997," he added.

Japan's donation of $5 million to the United Nations' voluntary trust fund and its pledge to support a study into appropriate technology for mine clearance operations was a guide for other donor nations, the UN mine expert added.
